title: Asian American History
description: Asian American histories from the Gold Rush, Railroads to World War II to present day. Immigration patterns, resistance stories, Constitution, Asians and Asian Americans in California. U.S. history from an Asian American perspective.
notes: Satisfies the American Institutions requirement in American history and California government. This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: Politics, Power, and Asian America
description: Asian American perspectives on politics and power. Considers activism, political participation, and laws related to Asian Americans. Ideals of the U.S. Constitution and its political institutions and processes.Formerly numbered:ASIAN 102ANote:Satisfies the American Institutions requirement in American history and United States Constitution. This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.Course Designations:American Institutions (AI)
notes: Satisfies the American Institutions requirement in American history and United States Constitution. This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: Introduction to Filipino American Studies
description: Introduction to Filipino American Studies to include culture, economics, history, governments, laws, and the artistic, intellectual, philosophical, political, and religious foundations for these structures.
notes: This course satisfies the Ethnics Studies [ES] requirement.

title: War, Empire, and the Asian American Experience
description: Introduction to major wars and conflicts involving Asian Americans as combatants and those affected by war. Key themes will include military campaigns, colonialism and imperialism, citizenship, refugees and immigration, families, memory, and gender.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement

title: Writing Composition and Rhetoric
description: Development of critical college-level writing and reading skills for the 21st century. Focus on communication and critical thinking skills through exploration of Asian American texts and readings.
notes: Satisfies Written Communication, CSU subarea A2. Not open to students with credit in a higher-numbered composition course or AFRAS 120 or AMIND 120 or CCS 111B or LING 100B or RWS 100 [or ECL 100] or RWS 105B.

title: Oral Communications and Public Speaking
description: Study and practice of oral communication skills and theories.
notes: Not open to students with credit in AFRAS 140, CCS 111A, or COMM 103

title: Asian Americans and Popular Culture
description: Interdisciplinary and intersectional approach to studying Asian Americans participation and representation in popular culture. Examination of historical contexts and power systems shaping Asian American identities within popular culture. Readings include a range of pop culture media and academic scholarship.
notes: This course satisfies the Ethnics Studies [ES] requirement.

title: Eating Asian America
description: Explore the people, practices, and dishes that make up contemporary Asian American food. Determine the important role that food plays in maintaining Asian American communities, cultures, and identities.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: Asian American Film and Media
description: Asian American experiences told through film and media. Independent films, documentaries, experimental, and social justice films.Formerly numbered:ASIAN 264Note:This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: Asian Americans and Mental Health
description: Exploration of diverse cultural, historical, and social contexts related to mental health in Asian American communities. Interdisciplinary and historical approaches to the study of Asian American experiences. Analysis of the role of institutions, policies, and power structures in Asian American experiences.
notes: This course satisfies the Ethnics Studies [ES] requirement.

title: Ethnocommunications: Creating Community Media
description: Introduction to community-centered media making in Asian American Studies: topics may include students analyze representation, practice interviewing, craft pitches, develop short media pieces.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: Gender, Sexuality, and Asian Americans
description: Feminism, gender, and sexuality in the lives and experiences of Asian Americans. Interdisciplinary, intersectional, theoretical, and applied approaches.Formerly numbered:ASIAN 301Note:This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: Asian American Communities
description: An overview of Asian American communities, cultures, and identities, with a focus on spatial and cultural formations.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: Korean American Experiences
description: An overview of Korean American communities, identities, issues, and cultural productions. Highlights the diversity of Korean American experiences, examining variations across race, gender, sexuality, and social class, among others.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: Asian Americans and Business
description: Asian American experiences in business, entrepreneurship, and labor force. Historical overview of how Asian Americans have contributed to business enterprises and endeavors. Topics may include Asian Americans in the Railroad, Agriculture, STEM, Education, and Healthcare industries.

title: Asian American Issues in the News
description: Exploration of current debates within the Asian American and transnational Asian American communities. Analysis of key debates involving Asian Americans in local, state, national, and international news. News sources include traditional media and new and emerging media.

title: Storytelling Techniques in Asian America
description: Overview of the techniques used by Asian American creative artists to tell a diverse set of stories related to the Asian American experience. Storytelling techniques may include those in film, novels, memoirs, and performance art. Analysis of storytelling techniques.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement

title: Asian American Experiences
description: Experiences of Asian/Pacific Islander Americans to include immigration, colonialism, imperialism, exclusion, citizenship, labor, family, community, gender, popular culture, refugees, multi-racial tensions, globalization, and resistance.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: Medical Humanities and Asian Americans
description: Exploration of the Asian American experience in the domain of disease, health, and medicine. Analysis of Asian American interactions and participation in medical discourses. Decolonization of medical humanities through centering Asian American experience. Topics include Asian American narratives of health.

title: Contemporary Issues in Filipino-American Communities
description: History of Philippines and Filipino immigration to US. Current issues in Filipino American communities to include labor, health, gender and sexuality, race relations, family culture and parenting, youth and the elderly, ethnic identity and empowerment.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.

title: Topics in Asian American Studies
description: Selected topics in American American Studies such as transnational, diaspora, computational, digital, community-engaged research methods.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific topic

title: Applied Praxis Projects
description: Analyzes real-world business or nonprofit projects through both Ethnic Studies and industry frameworks. Students develop career-ready skills while examining how standard practices shape economic outcomes for local communities.
notes: Open to all upper-division students.

title: Leadership and Asian Americans
description: Asian American perspectives on leadership and professional development. Exploration of Asian American participation and experiences with leadership. Topics may include Asian American cultural differences, Asian American representation and inclusion, and Asian American approaches to leadership. Personal leadership development.

title: Applying Asian American Studies
description: Application of Asian American Studies to a practical contemporary issues.
notes: This course satisfies the ethnic studies [ES] requirement.
